title: Global EV sales reach 1.8 million units in August 2026
author: Benchmark Team
text: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, specialising in EV and battery supply chain research and insights, reports that 1.83 million electric vehicles (EVs) were sold globally in August 2026, bringing year-to-date (YTD) 2026 EV sales to 13.4 million. In August 2026, EV sales increased by 2% year-on-year (y-o-y).Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Data Manager, Charles Lester, commented:"Global EV sales growth cooled sharply in August, rising just 2% year-on-year to 1.83 million units, as a deepening contraction in North America offset continued double-digit growth in Europe and an improving picture in China. Year-to-date sales now stand at 13.4 million units, up 4% on the same period last year."Europe remained the strongest performing region, with EV sales up 36% year-on-year in August, even as the region's holiday-driven slowdown that began in July carried into August, with sales down 15% month-on-month. The continued strength of subsidy-backed demand in the region's major markets pushed year-to-date growth up to 29%, from 28% at the end of July."China's year-on-year decline widened to 11% in August, from just 5% in July, though this reflects a tougher comparison against a stronger month last year rather than a fresh deterioration in demand, with sales actually rising 4% month-on-month. Chinese manufacturers continued to lean on overseas markets, with NEV exports hitting another record in August."North America's contraction deepened further in August, with sales down 33% year-on-year, the steepest decline of the year so far. As in July, this is a function of the market being compared against the pre-expiration buying rush seen in the US in August 2025, in the final weeks before the federal EV tax credit was removed at the end of September 2025, rather than a sign of a sudden new drop in demand."EuropeThe European EV market grew 36% year-on-year in August, building on the momentum seen through the first half of the year, though sales fell 15% month-on-month as the region's mid-summer lull, which began in July, extended into August across several major markets. This pushed year-to-date growth to 29%, up from 28% at the end of July.Spain's new "Auto+" subsidy scheme, which opened for applications on August 4 with retroactive eligibility back to January 1, 2026, has now had its first full month in operation. The centrally administered scheme, which offers a maximum base subsidy of EUR4,500 (USD5,190) per new EV passenger car and carries a EUR400 million (USD465 million) budget through 2026, replaced the regionally run "MOVES III" programme that expired at the end of 2025. Spain's EV market had already been growing in anticipation of the scheme (from 18% EV penetration in 2025 to 20% YTD 2026) and the opening of applications is expected to sustain that momentum through the rest of the year.Elsewhere, France, Germany and the UK, which together account for over half of all European EV sales, continued to benefit from a combination of purchase incentives, cheaper models and, in several markets, elevated fuel prices, extending the growth trend that saw France reach a record 41% EV penetration rate in August. North AmericaThe contraction of the North American EV market deepened further in August, with sales down 33% year-on-year, leaving the region down 21% year-to-date. This trend continues to be driven primarily by the US market, where EV share of new-vehicle sales has declined markedly relative to a year ago, when purchases surged ahead of the federal tax credit's expiration at the end of September 2025. Notably, US EV sales rose modestly on a month-over-month basis in August, even as the year-on-year comparison remained steeply negative. Several automakers posted significant year-on-year EV declines during the month, with hybrid vehicles capturing much of the share ceded by EVs. It is also worth noting that, given last September's comparable pre-expiration buying surge, the year-on-year comparison for September 2026 is likely to remain similarly pronounced.Canada's first six-month import window for lower-tariff Chinese-built EVs closed on August 31 with the quota under-subscribed: only 15,603 (mostly BEVs) of the 24,500 available permits were used, roughly 64% of the total. The unused balance of nearly 8,900 permits has carried over into the second window, which opened September 1 and now offers over 33,000 permits through to the end of February 2027. Take-up in the first window was concentrated among a small number of manufacturers already established in Canada, with several major Chinese brands yet to launch there.ChinaThe Chinese EV market's year-on-year decline widened to 11% in August, from 5% in July, even as sales rose 4% month-on-month. This left the market's year-to-date decline broadly unchanged at 12%. Despite the softer year-on-year comparison, EV penetration of China's overall passenger car market remains strong. at above 60% for the fourth consecutive month, with ICE sales down reflecting a continued shift toward electrified models on lower running costs even as overall demand remains subdued.Chinese manufacturers again turned to overseas markets to offset the softer domestic backdrop, with NEV exports surging over 150% year-on-year to a fresh monthly record of ~518,000 units in August, taking cumulative exports for the year to date past 3.3 million units. BYD retained its position as China's largest NEV exporter and has raised its full-year overseas sales target for the second time this year, reflecting the growing importance of export markets to Chinese automakers' growth plans.
